Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY token.mjs store.mjs engine.mjs stripe.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# license-keeper

After using this, you can now **sell a desktop app, plugin or CLI tool through
Stripe and have license keys issued, limited per machine, renewed with the
subscription and revoked on refund, on your own server**, which used to mean
paying a licensing platform per license or writing the plumbing yourself.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/license-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: generate an Ed25519 key pair, sign a test license and verify
  any key, in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: the license server. One Node process, **zero dependencies**,
  state in one JSON file. It receives Stripe webhooks, issues and emails keys,
  enforces machine limits, and answers your app's activation calls.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | License Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Keygen, Cryptlex, LicenseSpring, Paddle licensing | Paid, usually priced by licenses or activations; your customer list lives on their platform | Runs in your account, no per-license fee |
| Lemon Squeezy / Gumroad built-in keys | Easy, but keys are random strings only their API can check, and you pay the platform's cut | Keys are signed, so the app verifies them with no network |
| A script you write yourself | Easy to get wrong: replayed webhooks issuing twice, refunds not revoking, renewals not extending | Idempotent, tested state machine; dry-run by default |

Honest limits: no web portal for customers (they use the key from their email;
you can re-send it with `POST /v1/licenses/<id>/resend`), no tax or invoicing
(Stripe does that), no seat management beyond a machine count, and no
copy protection: a key is a deterrent, and anyone can patch software they
hold. It is **not yet run against live Stripe** by the author; use test mode
first.

## How a key works

`LK1.<claims>.<signature>`: the claims (product, email, plan, features, machine
limit, expiry) are JSON, signed with Ed25519. Your app embeds the **public
key** and verifies offline. See `token.mjs` (about 60 lines; WebCrypto, runs in
Node 20+ and browsers). In any language, verifying means checking an Ed25519
signature over the ASCII text `LK1.<claims>` (everything before the last dot)
with the raw 32-byte public key. The token format was cross-checked against
OpenSSL (`openssl pkeyutl -verify -rawin`) in the session that built it.

Subscriptions get a short-lived token (billing period plus `GRACE_DAYS`, default
3). The app calls `/v1/validate` now and then; while the subscription is paid
the server returns a fresh token with a later expiry, and once it lapses it
does not.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/license-keeper
node --test        # no network
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_test_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PLANS_JSON='{"price_123":{"product":"myapp","plan":"pro","features":["export"],"machines":2,"days":null}}' \
node server.mjs
```

It starts in **DRY_RUN** (the default): licenses are issued and logged, no
email goes out. First start generates a signing key pair and prints the public
key to embed in your app; it is stored in the state file (mode 600), or supply
`SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY` and `SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` yourself. **Back up the key.**

Setup in Stripe:

1. Restricted key: Checkout Sessions read, Subscriptions read. Nothing is written.
2. Webhook endpoint `https://<host>/webhook/stripe` for
   `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`,
   `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `charge.refunded`,
   `charge.dispute.created`.
3. `PLANS_JSON` maps each Stripe **price id** to what it grants:
   `{"product","plan","features":[],"machines":1,"days":null}`. `days: null` is
   perpetual; a number is a fixed term from purchase. Subscription prices follow
   the billing period instead. Quantity multiplies the machine count.

API (JSON):

| Call | Who | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/pubkey` | anyone | the public key |
| `POST /v1/activate` `{license, fingerprint, name}` | your app | registers the machine (up to the limit); returns a fresh token |
| `POST /v1/validate` `{license, fingerprint}` | your app | still valid? returns a fresh token |
| `POST /v1/deactivate` `{license, fingerprint}` | your app | frees the machine slot |
| `POST /v1/licenses` `{product,email,plan,machines,expiresAt}` | admin | issue by hand (PayPal, bank transfer, giveaways) |
| `GET /v1/licenses`, `GET /v1/summary` | admin | list, counts |
| `POST /v1/licenses/<id>/revoke`, `/resend`, `GET .../token` | admin | revoke, re-email, fetch the key |

Admin calls use `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY`. Public calls are rate limited
per address. Responses reveal a reason (`revoked`, `expired`, `machine-limit`,
`not-activated`).

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `ADMIN_KEY`, `PLANS_JSON` | required |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAIL_FROM` | key emails (needed when `DRY_RUN=false`) |
| `COMPANY_NAME` | signs the email |
| `GRACE_DAYS` | extra days after a paid period ends (default 3) |
| `SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY`, `SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | bring your own Ed25519 pair (base64url raw / PKCS8) |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`.
`render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a 1 GB
disk for the state file and generates `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's
side. State must survive restarts (licenses, activations and the signing key
live in it), so this uses an instance with a disk. Docker anywhere works too:
`docker build -t license-keeper . && docker run -p 8080:8080 -v lk:/data -e STATE=/data/state.json ... license-keeper`.
Put it behind HTTPS (Render does).

## Status and what is not verified

`node --test` passes against a fake Stripe, and the page was exercised in
headless Chromium (sign, verify, tamper detection, no axe violations). Not run
against live Stripe, and no real email sent. Email, refund and data-protection
rules differ by country; you are the operator and responsible for them.

Files: `token.mjs` (sign/verify; also runs in the browser), `store.mjs` (license
state machine), `engine.mjs` (Stripe events to licenses), `stripe.mjs` (webhook
verification, read calls), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell), `index.html` (key lab).
Related ventures, same buyer: [dunning-engine](../dunning-engine/),
[cancel-flow](../cancel-flow/), [mrr-pulse](../mrr-pulse/).

Support the project: <https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood>.

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   fly secrets set PLANS_JSON=...
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "license-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Sell your app with Stripe. Let the license keys take care of themselves.

A customer pays; a license key lands in their inbox; your app checks it offline with a public key you embed; a refund turns it off. License Keeper is the open-source server that does the middle of that, in your own account, with no per-license fee. Try the key format below. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing here is uploaded.

1. Make a key pair and sign a test license

2. Verify a license, offline

Result: not checked

ClaimValue

Change one character of the key and verify again: the signature fails. That is all an app needs to run offline.

3. Run the server yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo && cd fp-monorepo/ventures/license-keeper
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_live_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PLANS_JSON='{"price_123":{"product":"myapp","plan":"pro","machines":2,"days":null}}' \
RESEND_API_KEY=re_... MAIL_FROM="Acme <keys@example.com>" COMPANY_NAME=Acme \
node server.mjs          # DRY_RUN=true until you set DRY_RUN=false

Point a Stripe webhook at /webhook/stripe for checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, invoice.paid, customer.subscription.deleted, charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created. Your app posts /v1/activate with the license and a machine fingerprint. One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Questions

Why not just use Keygen, Lemon Squeezy or Gumroad license keys?

Hosted licensing services are good and quick to start, and Lemon Squeezy and Gumroad hand you a key as part of checkout. The catch is that the license data, the activation endpoint and the fees live on someone else's platform, and a random key can only be checked by calling that platform. License Keeper runs in your own account, signs keys with your own Ed25519 key so the app can verify them offline, and charges no per-license fee. If a hosted service already does the job for you, keep it.

Does the app need to call the server on every launch?

No. A license token is signed, so the app verifies it with the public key you embed and no network at all. It only calls the server to activate a machine, to refresh a token that is about to expire (subscriptions), and to learn about a revocation. Between those calls your customers can work offline.

What happens if I lose the signing key or the server goes down?

Tokens already issued keep verifying offline for as long as they are valid, because verification needs only the public key. Back up the state file: it holds the signing key unless you supply your own with SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY, and without that key you cannot issue or refresh licenses that your embedded public key accepts.

How are refunds and chargebacks handled?

A full refund or a dispute on the original payment revokes the license. Apps that validate online see the revocation on their next check; a token already cached offline works until it expires, so use short-lived tokens for subscriptions and treat perpetual offline tokens as honour-system after a refund.

Is it safe to try?

It starts in dry-run mode: it issues and logs licenses but sends no email until you set DRY_RUN=false. Try it with a Stripe test-mode key first. It never writes to Stripe.

Same buyer, other jobs: Dunning Engine recovers failed subscription payments, Cancel Flow handles voluntary cancellations, MRR Pulse shows MRR, churn and net revenue retention, Feedback Board collects feature requests, Waitlist Keeper runs a referral waitlist before launch, Referral Keeper pays affiliates commission on Stripe sales, and Visit Keeper shows which traffic source brings paying customers.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. License keys are a deterrent, not copy protection: a determined user can remove checks from software they hold. You are the operator, responsible for your own Stripe account, your terms with customers, refunds, and the consumer-protection and data-protection rules where you and they live. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# The key you paste needs Checkout Sessions: read and Subscriptions: read. This server never writes to Stripe.
services:
  - type: web
    name: license-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/license-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/license-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
        sync: false
      - key: PLANS_JSON
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: RESEND_API_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: MAIL_FROM
        sync: false
